headline: Isomorphic Labs' new AI engine more than doubles AlphaFold 3's accuracy in drug design
summary: The Isomorphic Labs Drug Design Engine (IsoDDE) significantly improves protein-ligand structure prediction, identifying novel binding pockets and outperforming previous models like AlphaFold 3.
details: Isomorphic Labs has unveiled its Drug Design Engine (IsoDDE), a unified computational system for drug discovery. It significantly surpasses AlphaFold 3 in predictive accuracy and introduces new capabilities for real-world drug development.

IsoDDE more than doubles AlphaFold 3's accuracy on challenging protein-ligand structure prediction benchmarks. It also predicts small molecule binding-affinities with greater accuracy than gold-standard physics-based methods, at a fraction of the time and cost.

A key advancement is IsoDDE's ability to accurately identify novel binding pockets on target proteins using only the amino acid sequence as input. This addresses a major limitation of previous models, which struggled to generalize to unexplored regions of biomolecular space.

The engine demonstrates a step change in generalizing to protein-ligand structures highly dissimilar to its training set. On the 'Runs N' Poses' benchmark, it shows improved modeling of complex events like induced fits and the opening of cryptic pockets.

Beyond small molecules, IsoDDE also provides a significant accuracy leap for modeling antibody-antigen interfaces. It outperforms AlphaFold 3 by 2.3x and Boltz-2 by 19.8x in high-fidelity regimes on a novel test set.

Crucially, IsoDDE shows remarkable performance on the CDR-H3 loop, the most variable and difficult part of an antibody to predict. This capability effectively unlocks new possibilities for de novo antibody design, advancing therapeutic modalities.

headline_marked: [[Kaiser nurses say AI, surveillance worsen jobs, patient care]] with strict call time limits
headline: Kaiser nurses say AI, surveillance worsen jobs, patient care with strict call time limits
summary: Kaiser Permanente nurses report that strict call time limits and AI-powered surveillance are hindering their ability to provide compassionate patient care, leading to performance criticisms. This impacts both nurse well-being and patient outcomes.
details: Kaiser Permanente nurses are raising alarms over workplace surveillance and AI tools, which they say are compromising their ability to deliver quality patient care. Nurses report facing criticism and performance evaluations for spending more than 15 minutes on calls, even in critical situations.

Beyond call length tracking, Kaiser uses software to predict unproductivity and assess how quickly calls are answered. AI systems are also employed to rate nurses' empathy and tone of voice, adding pressure to interactions.

These concerns emerge as the California Nurses Association (CNA) begins contract negotiations with Kaiser, with AI policies expected to be a central issue. Nurses previously went on strike against AI in March and picketed last fall.

California lawmakers are also addressing the issue, considering bills to regulate AI in the workplace. One proposed bill aims to protect doctors and nurses from retaliation for overriding automated care recommendations.

Kaiser Permanente, California's largest private employer, defends its AI use, stating it prioritizes patient safety and does not use "average handle time" for performance assessment. The company's practices could set significant precedents for AI management in healthcare.

Raquel Alvarez Sanchez, a Kaiser advice nurse, recounted a call with a suicidal patient that lasted over an hour, knowing it would negatively impact her performance metrics. She fears such pressures could lead nurses to quit or retire early.

Another anonymous nurse described cutting short a compassionate conversation with a terminally ill patient, fearing a reprimand for "going off script." This highlights the conflict between humanistic care and AI-driven performance targets.
